2026-11-02.meal: Veggie fajitas (plus a fajita bowl for Jess's lunch tomorrow)
2026-11-02.note: Moved from Sunday. Make one extra portion for Jess's work lunch on Tuesday as a fajita bowl.

ingredients: 1 microwave rice pouch (for the lunch bowl)
To serve: salsa, soured cream, lettuce, avocado
steps: Fry the onions and peppers in the oil for 8–10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the beans, sweetcorn and a splash of water. Take out Mathilda's portion now, keeping it plain.
Stir the fajita seasoning through the rest and simmer for 5 minutes.
Spoon one portion into a lunch box for tomorrow and let it cool.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave. Fill with the filling, cheese and toppings, fold and serve.

For the lunch bowl: once cool, put the rice pouch (unopened) and the filling in the fridge. At work, microwave the filling until piping hot, heat the rice, and top with cheese, lettuce, salsa and a dollop of soured cream (pack the cold toppings in a separate pot).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers mild with no seasoning. Cool the lunch portion within an hour and keep it in the fridge overnight.

2026-11-03.meal: Slow-cooker sausage & bean casserole with mash
2026-11-03.note: This week's one meat night. Hull hockey training 6–7pm (Hymers College) plus travel. Slow cooker on by 11am, so tea's ready for whoever's not driving and stays warm for the rest.

ingredients: 400g tin cannellini or butter beans, drained
Mash (fresh potatoes or microwave pouches) or crusty bread, to serve
steps: Brown the sausages in the oil in a frying pan for 5 minutes, then put them in the slow cooker.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then tip into the slow cooker.
Add the carrots, tomatoes, beans, purée and stock. Stir and season.
Cover and cook on low for 6–7 hours (or high for 3–4), until the sausages are cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Make the mash (or heat the pouches) when you're ready to eat.
Serve the casserole over the mash, or with crusty bread.
recipe.tip: Turn the slow cooker to 'keep warm' once it's done so it's ready for whoever's back late. Mathilda: slice her sausages into coins and check they're cooked through.

2026-11-04.meal: Air-fryer crispy gnocchi with roasted tomatoes, courgette & pesto
2026-11-04.note: Hockey Academy night 6:15–7:45pm (The Lindum). Ready in 20 minutes either side of the run.

ingredients: Grated parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, or torn mozzarella, to serve
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C.
Toss the gnocchi, courgette and cherry tomatoes in the oil with a pinch of salt.
Air fry for 12–15 minutes, shaking the basket every 5 minutes, until the gnocchi is golden and crisp and the tomatoes have burst. (Do it in two batches if your basket is small.)
Tip into a big bowl and toss with the pesto, and the rocket or spinach if using.
Serve with cheese on top.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: give her some plain crispy gnocchi and tomatoes before the pesto goes in, with a little cheese. Check the pesto label if anyone's avoiding nuts.

2026-11-05.meal: Tomato soup & cheese toasties (plus a flask for the fireworks)
2026-11-05.note: Bonfire night, out to watch the fireworks. Super quick and warming, with a flask of soup to take with you.

ingredients: 2 x 600g cartons fresh tomato soup (or 4 tins)
8 slices bread (the kids' bread or the sourdough)
Butter or spread, for the bread
steps: Heat the soup in a pan, stirring, until it's piping hot (about 5 minutes).
While it heats, butter the outsides of the bread and make 4 cheese sandwiches.
Cook the toasties in a dry frying pan for 2–3 minutes a side until golden and melted, or air fry at 190°C for 6–8 minutes, turning halfway.
Cut the toasties into soldiers for dunking and serve with mugs of soup.
Fill a flask with the leftover hot soup to take to the fireworks (warm the flask with boiling water first so it stays hot).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her toastie into small fingers and let the soup cool a little before she has it. Pack a few mugs or cups for the flask.
